domain.text: Conflict-resolution automation for GitHub task PRs, including watcher dispatch, model selection, safety limits, escalation, and approval carry.

impressions.text: The delivery implemented conflict handling for both live-worker and session-less paths, with tests and reported local checks covering safety gates, CI, verification, and approval outcomes.

Live testing confirmed the worker resolved a real conflict after receiving the CONFLICT line; the run exposed premature model restoration, which the worker fixed and tested, though the initial missing switch was not independently diagnosed.

The disposable fixer selected glm-flash and resolved the conflict, then added an unrelated changelog commit; the hunk proof correctly blocked it, and the prompt was tightened to prohibit extra commits, without a subsequent live run of that tightened prompt.
An earlier live run falsely escalated an already-current PR after GitHub returned a no-new-commits error; the preflight and error handling were corrected and regression-tested.
Automatic merging of an owner-approved PR was covered by tests but not exercised live; the orchestrator said it would monitor the first real use.
